Thanks Alex — good questions. Short answers up front, then next steps: 

1) Shared Hosted API tail behavior:
- Typical p99 under normal load: 250–400ms for the models we demoed.
- During noisy-neighbor events, we've seen p99 spikes up to ~700–900ms on hosts that are not pinned; those are rare and we have automated fallback to compatible model variants to preserve availability.
- For customer-facing low-latency SLOs (p95 < 120ms), we rely on prefix caching, continuous batching limits, and regional routing; many customers meet p95 targets on Hosted when workload is latency-sensitive and steady.

2) Dedicated isolation model:
- Dedicated means GPU pools reserved to your tenancy with node/pod-level isolation. You get tenant-affinity at the hardware level; noisy neighbor jitter is reduced to <10–15% of the spikes seen on shared hosts in our benchmarks. We provide SLA-backed p95 latency targets and a documented incident response playbook.

3) Migration path to Private VPC/on-prem:
- Migration is supported with minimal API changes; you can pin model versions and routing rules. Data plane differences (networking, KMS) require some infra work, but we've migrated three customers in the last year with a 2–4 week cutover.

Next steps:
- Can you share the telemetry snapshot and your SLO doc? I created a template (attached) — if you send the raw CSV we can run a quick cost & mode recommendation and do a targeted performance review.
- If you'd like, Marissa (solutions infra) can join a 30-min infra deep-dive next week to walk through Dedicated sizing and SLAs.

Attachments: finpay_sample_telemetry_template.csv, redwood_shared_vs_dedicated_onepager.pdf
